paragraphs: He further merited to learn from Resh Lakish, as in Beitzah chapter 1, halakhah 9: he asked Resh Lakish, 'What is the law regarding grinding (לשחוק) kondiṭon on a festival day?' He said to him, 'Give me and I will drink.' This statement is not found in our Yerushalmi, but it is indeed cited thus in the Ran, Beitzah chapter 1, printed locator קפו:.[^1][^2]

And his principal teacher was R' Ze’ira (printed: ר״ז א׳), as in Sotah chapter 3, halakhah 1: 'R' Ze’ira brought R' Yitzchak Atusha, and he recited it for him.' And Peah chapter 8, halakhah 4: 'He said before R' Ze’ira in the name of the school of Rabbi Yannai.'[^3]

And he had a son named Rabbi Chiyya, as in Terumot chapter 10, halakhah 6: 'R' Yirmeyah instructed R' Yitzchak Atusha,' and some say: 'R' Chiyya son of R' Yitzchak Atusha.' The author of Seder HaDorot wrote that he served as a reciter (tanna) for R' Abba bar Memel, but was mistaken in this, as I explained in his entry.[^4]

notes.text: The contextual expansions R' Ze’ira and R' Yitzchak Atusha follow the full names in the inspected Sotah and Peah passages cited below; the father–son names also appear in Terumot. The extra א׳ after Hyman’s ר״ז is retained without deciding whether it labels an earlier namesake. רשב״ל is read conventionally as Resh Lakish and ס״הד as Seder HaDorot. The person meant by Hyman’s ‘his entry’ has not been established here.

‘Grinding’ translates לשחוק in the drink-preparation context. The complete [Yerushalmi Beitzah 1:9:3](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Beitzah.1.9.3), Guggenheimer’s Hebrew edition (De Gruyter, 1999–2015), discusses grinding ingredients and konditon. Its speakers are Yitzchak Dihava and R' Yohanan, unlike the names in Hyman’s report. It supports the sense of the verb, not the identity of the speakers or the presence of Hyman’s version. His absence claim is retained as referring to that version. The Ran reference and printed locator קפו: remain unverified and unconverted.

The complete [Yerushalmi Sotah 3:1:5](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Sotah.3.1.5), Guggenheimer’s edition, says that R' Ze’ira brought R' Yitzchak Atushiyya to recite a teaching. It supports the recitation sense and the names used in the English. [Peah 8:4:4](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Peah.8.4.4) contains the report before R' Ze’ira in the name of the school of R' Yannai. Hyman’s final claim about serving Abba bar Memel is translated as a reciter’s role, not a newly asserted teacher–pupil relationship.

The inspected [Terumot 10:6:11](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Terumot.10.6.11), Guggenheimer’s edition, explicitly names R' Chiyya as the son of R' Yitzchak Atushiyya. It does not contain the exact ruling/version Hyman quotes, which remains unverified. Hyman’s wording, alternative recipient and parent–child relationship are retained. His criticism of Seder HaDorot remains his own attributed claim.

The heading’s Rabbi Yitzchak, the Peah school of Rabbi Yannai, and the introductory statement naming his son Rabbi Chiyya have explicit full-title support in the matching named passages. R' preserves the ambiguous titles in Hyman’s exact Terumot ruling and its alternative wording, which the checked paragraph does not contain, and in the unchecked Seder HaDorot claim about Abba bar Memel. An explicit Rabbi elsewhere in a paragraph is not transferred to a different quoted occurrence. Other neutral R' forms retain the source’s abbreviation without changing the names or reported relationships.
